items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: Stuff Smith came out there with his band, with Cozy Cole and Clyde Hart and Mack -- Jonah Jones.

ctx.x: Well, what about the extra-curricular thing. You know, what was the scene like? Where did you go after the gig? Was there still --

Oh, there wasn't too many places out there. Well, we did -- now, during the time I was out there Art Tatum came out there, Stuff Smith came out there with his band, with Cozy Cole and Clyde Hart and Mack -- Jonah Jones. And they were playing at a place called The Famous Door.

Now, when they came out there we used to go out at night with Stuff and me and Clyde and Jonah and all of them. We used to go around places like after hour spots and we would jam and play. And this is one of the big things that made Stuff mess up his career because when he first came out there Stuff was very hot. He'd come from 52nd Street and they had pictures lined up and everything for him to do. And we were hanging out after they got off.

items.title: 53342_Cozy Cole oral history interview
items.q: So I guess Eddie and them went up there and got him and took him home and I didn't hear no more about him.

ctx.x: sit down there and liable to cause something else, and in this place nobody knows Don Bias, and they care less who Don Bias is really. And he's got his money out, about $800, $900 on him, in one of these big long pocketbooks and had it flashing out his back pocket." I said, "Don, things aren't like they used to be. When you was up here 24 years ago they'd kill you for that amount of money. Now they'll kill you with people looking for that amount of money nowadays." So I had to get a cab and send him home and I…

did a couple more concerts and got a few more dollars in his pocket, then's when he started getting wild, drinking again and thinking that Harlem was the same place that he left 24 years ago and it wasn't, until somebody called Eddie Barefield and says, 'oh man, come up here and get your man. He's up here at Basie's place, which was 132nd and 7th Avenue and he's up here going wild, flashing his money and all that.' So I guess Eddie and them went up there and got him and took him home and I didn't hear no more…
Well I guess Art Blakey had him tour with his group for a little while.
